source.place: Tag 07P5 proof, explicit bounded-monomial and residue grouping arguments

proof.text: Split each finite-variable exponent coordinatewise into a p-divisible exponent and a residue below p, using quotient and remainder. For a power series phi and an index (q,e), construct the column as the actual coefficient function whose value at a p-divisible exponent a is the q coordinate under b.repr of coeff(a+e,phi), embedded from K into k, and whose other coefficients are zero. These columns have coefficients in K and p-divisible support. Comparing coefficients using monomial multiplication and basis reconstruction proves that phi is the finite sum of the columns times the coefficient-residue monomials.

For each monomial y^g phi in the finite polynomial support, split g=d+h with d divisible by p and h a residue vector. Apply the series decomposition to phi. Each monomial y^d times a series column belongs to S by hS; multiplying it by the displayed residue monomial with index (q,e,h) gives the corresponding term of y^g phi. Every polynomial monomial therefore lies in the S-span, and the finite polynomial support decomposition proves spanning. This avoids constructing a polynomial column by regrouping all polynomial exponents.

For a finite S-linear combination of the residue monomials, compare its coefficient at (a+e,g+h), where a and g are divisible by p. The monomial coefficient formulas and support divisibility force any contributing summand to have residues exactly (e,h): reducing the exponent equation modulo p and using bounds below p proves this. Its coefficient is the scalar column coefficient times b(q). Applying b.repr and taking the q coordinate recovers precisely that scalar column coefficient. In a zero relation this is zero at every divisible exponent; hS makes every other coefficient zero. Extensionality of power series, polynomials, subring elements, and finitely supported functions proves linear independence. Apply Module.Basis.mk to independence and spanning; Module.Basis.mk_apply gives the required displayed basis values.

title: Residue monomials give a basis
statement: Let $p>0$ be a natural number, $k$ a field, $K\subset k$ a subfield [def-weil-field], $Q$ a finite set, and $b:Q\to k$ a $K$-basis [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Let $n,m\ge0$ and $A=k[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]][y_1,\ldots,y_m]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series, def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Let $S\subset A$ be a subring consisting exactly of elements whose coefficients lie in $K$ and whose nonzero coefficients have each series and polynomial exponent divisible by $p$. Then $A$ has an $S$-basis indexed by $Q\times\{0,\ldots,p-1\}^n\times\{0,\ldots,p-1\}^m$, whose value at $(q,e,h)$ is $b(q)\prod_i x_i^{e_i}\prod_j y_j^{h_j}$.

lean.statement:
theorem powerSeriesResidueMonomialBasis
    (p : ℕ) (hp : 0 < p)
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (K : Subfield k)
    (Q : Type v) [Finite Q] (b : Module.Basis Q K k)
    (n m : ℕ)
    (S : Subring (MvPolynomial (Fin m) (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) k)))
    (hS : ∀ f, f ∈ S ↔
      ∀ (a : Fin n →₀ ℕ) (g : Fin m →₀ ℕ),
        MvPowerSeries.coeff a (MvPolynomial.coeff g f) ∈ K ∧
        (MvPowerSeries.coeff a (MvPolynomial.coeff g f) ≠ 0 →
          (∀ i, p ∣ a i) ∧ (∀ j, p ∣ g j))) :
    ∃ B : Module.Basis (Q × (Fin n → Fin p) × (Fin m → Fin p)) S
      (MvPolynomial (Fin m) (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) k)),
      ∀ q, B q =
        MvPolynomial.C (MvPowerSeries.C (b q.1) *
          ∏ i : Fin n, MvPowerSeries.X i ^ (q.2.1 i : ℕ)) *
        ∏ j : Fin m, MvPolynomial.X j ^ (q.2.2 j : ℕ)
